answer: In a PoA meadow of agents, each newcomer must obtain vouches signed by three existing nodes whose reputations were earned at the network’s dawn. The voucher contract stores a relic hash of every vouch; if any vouched node is later proved to be a Sybil, the contract automatically revokes its signatures and deducts stake from the endorsers, making their trust score drop. An attacker therefore pays the full stake of every endorsing node for each fake identity, scaling linearly with the number of required vouches.
